THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the petitioner seeking enhancement of compensation passed by the Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Bidar (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.569/2013 dated 21.01.2016.
2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are:
On 6-10-2011 when the petitioner was proceeding in an Appe autorickshaw bearing its Reg.No.KA-38/3917 as a passenger from his village Kamthana towards his shop at Gandhi Gunj in Bidar.

The driver of the autorickshaw was driving the same in a high speed with negligent manner and in due course of the same at about 10-30 a.m. while he was so proceeding near Chidri by-pass ring road Chowk at Bidar, lost the control over the same and in the result of which, it is toppled down.

Because of this accident,
the claimant was being inmate of the said auto sustained grievous injuries to his leg,
forehead and chest.
Immediately, he was shifted to Prayavi hospital at Bidar, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 6-10-2011 till 9-10-2011.
After discharge, he went to Sholapur and took treatment as an inpatient in Yeshodra hospital from 10-10-2011 till 25-10-2011.
He spent more than Rs.2 lakhs towards medical and other expenses.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and running the commission agency having Adat shop in Gandhi Gunj Bidar.
He was also an agriculturist.

Thus,
his income is not less than Rs.25,000/- per month.

His age was 40 years and because of the accidental injuries, he is unable to sit continuously and there is disfiguration of his great toe and thereupon he unable to walk and suffering from permanent disability and thereby lost his income and future income.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has been permanently disabled and lost source of income.
Thereby causing dent to him financially, mentally and physically.
Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

2
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
7. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal after considering the notional monthly income of the claimant awarded compensation of Rs.78,400/-.
8. Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.
9. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.
He further submits that the tribunal has not passed any compensation towards disability though the doctor has given evidence and tribunal has awarded meager compensation.
On all these grounds sought for allowing the appeal and consequently seeks to enhance the compensation.

10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2-insurer supports the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.
11. It is seen that the respondents had not challenged the judgment and award and therefore accepted the liability to pay the compensation.
Insofar as claim for compensation is concerned

,
injuries show that petitioner had suffered permanent disability.
12. A perusal of the impugned judgment at paragraph Nos.13 to 14 wherein the tribunal has observed as under;
"14.P.w-2/Dr. V.Bulgundi is an orthopedic surgeon in Bidar He issued disability certificate as per Ex.P8 after lapse of 3 years on the basis of records.
Looking to the Ex.P8, it appears that he was not treated the petitioner except issuing the said certificate as per Ex.P8.
Even it is admitted by P.w-2 in the beginning line of his cross-examination.
Of course, Pw-2 reiterated the contents of Ex.P8 in his chief examination and stated his opinion about permanent disability to the left lower limb to the extent of 25% and to the whole body 20%.
However, during the course of cross-examination he admitted that as per Ex.P5 the injuries i.e." degloving injuries to left foot over 1st and 2nd web space is mentioned as simple injury."

during the course of his cross- examination, deposed that he is continued his business and there is no material about the proof of previous income and present income to believe him that there is a loss of future income as deposed by P.w-1.
Thus, I am of the view that looking to the injury suffered to him, the disability spoken by P.w-2 appears to be exaggerated and the same is not at all affected to the profession of petitioner.
In view of this opinion, I discarded the claim of loss of income due to disablement.
13. A careful scrutiny of the finding given by the tribunal, It is clear that the tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record regarding loss of future income.

3 14.

Considering the nature of injuries and medical evidence, with regard to the other heads are concerned, I am of the considered opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re-determined and re-calculated as under:-
 Heads Awarded by Awarded by  the tribunal this Court  Pain & suffering Rs.10,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs.44,400/- Rs.44,400/-

Attendant charges Rs.4,000/- Rs.4,000/-
 Food, nutrition and diet Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,000/-
 Conveyance charges Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,000/-

Loss of amenities Rs.10,000/- Rs.25,000/-
 Laid up period ---- Rs.5,000/-
 Total Rs.78,400/- Rs.1,03,400/-
15.

In view of the above, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.569/2013 dated 21.01.2016 is modified.
The compensation of Rs.78,400/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.1,03,400/-.
(c) The respondent-No.2-insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
(d) The respondent No.2-insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(e) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.

Sd/-
